common_name: Little John Bottlebrush (Dwarf Compact Red-Flowered Bottlebrush)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring after frost danger passes in well-drained soil in full sun; Little John is a dwarf, compact bottlebrush cultivar reaching only 2-3 feet, well suited to smaller gardens and containers.

directions: Plant in well-drained soil in full sun; bottlebrush tolerates heat, humidity, and short dry spells once established, though it does not tolerate wet feet. Little John stays notably compact and dense for a bottlebrush, reaching only about two to three feet tall and wide, yet produces the same brilliant red, bristly bottlebrush-shaped flower spikes as full-sized cultivars, blooming heavily in spring with lighter repeat flushes through the warm season and drawing hummingbirds reliably. Its dwarf, tidy habit fits foundation plantings, containers, and small garden beds where larger bottlebrush shrubs would be out of scale. Prune lightly after the main spring bloom to shape, and protect from hard freezes in the coolest parts of its range.

common_name: Blush Pink Loropetalum (Soft Pink Compact Fringe Flower)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in well-drained, slightly acidic to acidic soil in full sun to partial shade; Blush Pink is a compact loropetalum with softer green-tinted foliage and pale pink fringe flowers, a gentler look than the deep-purple cultivars.

directions: Plant in well-drained, slightly acidic to acidic soil in full sun to partial shade; good drainage is essential, since waterlogged soils cause rapid root rot. Blush Pink offers a softer look within the loropetalum family, with green-tinted foliage rather than the deep purple-red of most popular cultivars, paired with soft pale pink fringe flowers in spring and intermittently through summer and fall, giving a gentler, more pastel effect useful for blending with green-foliage companions. Its compact, mounding habit fits foundation plantings and shrub borders without requiring constant shearing to control size. Loropetalums are among the most heat- and humidity-tolerant ornamental shrubs for the Gulf South and are largely free of serious pest and disease problems; no pruning is required, but plants respond well to light shaping immediately after the main spring bloom.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; Jack Frost bears foliage margined in bright white, a variegated selection of Chinese privet grown as a tough, easy-care hedge or accent shrub.

directions: Plant in well-drained, average soil in full sun to partial shade. Jack Frost bears leaves boldly margined in crisp white around a gray-green center, a striking variegated pattern that brightens a mixed border or hedge planting year-round, since the foliage is evergreen. It tolerates heat, drought, and poor soil with ease and needs only occasional shearing to maintain a tidy shape as a hedge, screen, or specimen accent. Its bright, variegated foliage provides ornamental value distinct from solid-green privet hedging, working well as a lighter-colored backdrop for darker-leaved shrubs and perennials.
